segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Hi Jeannie. How's it going? ,IEANNIE: Oh, hello Dan. Pretty well, thanks. Have you managedto get the money for the course yet?

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Yes, that's all sorted out now, thanks. It took long enough, though. It was practically a year ago that I applied to my local council for a grant, and it took them six months to turn me down.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: That's really slow.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: And I thought I was eligible for governmentfunding, but it seems I was mistaken. So then I asked the boss of the company I used to work for if they would sponsor me, and much to my surprise, he said they'd make a contribution.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: But what about college grants and scholarships? There must be some you could apply for.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Yes, there are, but they're all so small that I decided to leave them until I was desperate.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Uhuh.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: And in fact I didn't need to apply. My parents had been saying that as I already had a job, I ought to support myself through college. But in the end they took pity on me, so now I've just about got enough.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: That's good.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: So now I can put a bit of effort into meeting people — I haven't had time so far. Any suggestions?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: What about joining some college clubs?

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Oh right. You joined several didn't you?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Yes, I'm in the drama club. It's our first performance next week, so we're rehearsing frantically, and I've got behind with my work, but it's worth it. I'm hoping to be in the spring production, too.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: I've never liked acting. Are you doing anything else?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: I enjoyed singing when I was at school, so I joined a group when I came to college. I don't think the conductor stretches us enough, though, so I'll give up after the next concert. And I also joined the debating society. It's fun, but with all the rehearsing I'm doing, something has to go, and I'm afraid that's the one.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Do you do any sports?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Yes, I'm in one of the hockey teams. I'm not very good, but I'd really miss it if I stopped. I decided to try tennis when I came to college, and I'm finding it pretty tough going. I'm simply not fit enough.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Nor me. I think I'll give that a miss!

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: I'm hoping it'll help me to build up my stamina, but it'll probably be a long haul.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Good luck.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Thanks.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: How are you finding the course?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: I wish we had more seminars.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: What? I'd have thought we had more than enough already.All those people saying clever things that I could never think of - it's quite interesting,but I wonder if I'm clever enough to be doing this course.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: I find it helpful to listen to the other people. I like the way we're exploring the subject, and working towardsgetting insight into it.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: How do you get on with your tutor? I don't think I'm on the same wavelengthas mine, so I feel I'm not getting anything out of the tutorials. It would be more productiveto read a book instead.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Oh, mine's very demanding.She gives me lots of feedbackand advice, so I've got much better at writing essays.And she's helping me plan my - revisionfor the end-of-yearexams.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Do tell me, I always strugglewith revision.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Well, the first thing is to find out exactly what’s required in the exams.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Mm. Would it help to get hold of some past papers?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Yes. They'll help to make it clear.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Right, I'll do that. Then what?

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Then you can sort out your revision priorities,based on what's most likely to come up. I put these on a card, and read them through regularly.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Uhuh.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: But that isn't enough in itself. You also need a timetable,to see how you can fit everythingin, in the time available.Then keep it in front of you while you're studying.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: I've done that before, but it hasn't helped me!

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Maybe you need to do somethingdifferentevery day, so if you break down your revision into small tasks, and allocatethem to specific days, there's more incentiveto tackle them. With big topics you're more likely to put off starting.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Good idea.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: And as I revise each topic I write a single paragraph about it - then later I can read it through quickly, and it helps fix things in my mind.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: That's brilliant.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: I also write answers to questions for the exam practice. It's hard to make myself do it, though!

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Well, I'll try. Thanks a lot, Jeannie. That's a great help.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: No problem.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: See you around.

segments.speaker: JEANNIE
segments.en: Bye.
